note: β3 agonists were repositioned from obesity to OAB; rat bladder is far less sensitive than human, so human strips plus rat, dog and rhesus cystometry carried the prediction.
label: Overactive bladder (β3)

engagement.model: Human and rat isolated bladder strips
engagement.note: Mirabegron relaxed carbachol-contracted human bladder strips (EC50 0.78 µM) but needed 6.5× more in rat strips; no patient target-engagement read-out published.
engagement.short: Human strips relax; rat needs 6.5× more
engagement.quote: EC50 values of YM178 and isoproterenol in rat bladder strips precontracted with 10(-6) M CCh were 5.1 and 1.4 microM, respectively, whereas those in human bladder strips precontracted with 10(-7) M CCh were 0.78 and 0.28 microM, respectively.
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level. No source puts a bladder target-engagement read-out in patients beside the strip data. Di Salvo 2017 (doi 10.1124/jpet.116.237313) proposed circulating glycerol/fatty acids as a β3 engagement biomarker in rat and rhesus and wrote 'The translation of our observation to the clinic has yet to be determined'. Phase 3 voided-volume gains (Nitti 2013; Staskin 2020) are consistent with detrusor relaxation but were never compared with the model, so untested, not same.

dose.model: Cloned human β3 cAMP assay and bladder strips
dose.note: Human β3 cAMP EC50 22.4 nM; rat strips 6.5× less sensitive than human. No published comparison of model potency with clinical exposure found.
dose.short: Rat tissue 6.5× less sensitive than human
dose.quote: YM178 increased cyclic AMP accumulation in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells expressing human beta3-adrenoceptor (AR). The half-maximal effective concentration (EC50) value was 22.4 nM.
dose.judgement: Hatanaka 2013 (doi 10.1007/s00210-012-0821-4) found cloned rat β3 EC50 19 nM, equal to human 22.4 nM, so the species gap sits in the tissue (rat strip 290 nM passive tension, 5.1 µM precontracted), not the receptor. Michel & Korstanje 2016 (review, doi 10.1016/j.pharmthera.2016.01.007) list species differences as a translational challenge but are a pointer, not a source. The FDA clinical pharmacology review (202611Orig1s000ClinPharmR.pdf) exceeded the fetch size limit and was not read.

efficacy.note: Mirabegron 3 mg/kg i.v. cut the frequency of filling-induced bladder contractions in anaesthetised rats without blunting amplitude; solabegron raised micturition threshold in dogs.
efficacy.short: Rat cystometry: fewer contractions, voiding intact
efficacy.quote: In in vivo study, YM178 at a dose of 3 mg/kg i.v. decreased the frequency of rhythmic bladder contraction induced by intravesical filling with saline without suppressing its amplitude in anesthetized rats.
efficacy.judgement: Solabegron's pivotal model was the anaesthetised dog (Hicks 2007, doi 10.1124/jpet.107.125757: raised the volume needed to evoke micturition after acetic-acid irritation without impairing voiding); vibegron's was rhesus cystometry (Di Salvo 2017).

efficacy.note: Solabegron 125 mg cut incontinence episodes and micturitions and raised voided volume in 258 women with OAB, the direction the animal models predicted.
efficacy.short: Solabegron cut micturitions in OAB women
efficacy.quote: Solabegron 125 mg treatment also showed statistically significant reductions from baseline to weeks 4 and 8 in micturitions over 24 h and a statistically significant increase from baseline to week 8 in urine volume voided.
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level. Ohlstein opens with 'β-Adrenoceptor agonists are effective in animal models of bladder dysfunction' and reports the patient result in the same paper, but it is a premise, not a side-by-side comparison, hence comparison_stated false and confidence medium. Mirabegron ARIES (Nitti 2013, doi 10.1016/j.juro.2012.10.017, print 2013, epub 2012-10-16, NCT00662909 results posted 2012-10-17: micturitions −1.66 vs −1.05 placebo per 24 h) and vibegron EMPOWUR (Staskin 2020, doi 10.1097/JU.0000000000000807, NCT03492281 results posted 2021-03-04: −1.8 vs −1.3) confirm without changing status. Ritobegron's Phase 3 NCT01004315 (Kissei) is marked completed with no results posted and its extension NCT01003405 withdrawn; its failure is known only from the sponsor, so no primary source supports contra or neg. Solabegron's 2018-19 Velicept Phase 2b trials NCT03594058/NCT03475706 likewise have no posted results. Ohlstein's trial NCT00343486 has no posted results, so registry_date is null.

safety.note: Mirabegron and solabegron showed ≤10% β1/β2 intrinsic activity at 10 µM on cloned receptors, predicting no cardiovascular liability; no patient comparison yet.
safety.short: Cloned receptors predict no β1 effect
safety.quote: The ratio of intrinsic activities of YM178 versus maximal response induced by isoproterenol (nonselective beta-AR agonist) was 0.8 for human beta3-ARs, 0.1 for human beta1-ARs, and 0.1 for human beta2-ARs.
safety.judgement: Solabegron: Hicks 2007 reports a maximum β1/β2 response <10% of isoproterenol at 10,000 nM. Ritobegron: Maruyama 2012 (doi 10.1007/s00210-012-0755-x) adds anaesthetised-rat haemodynamics, 'without affecting heart rate and only slightly lowering mean blood pressure'.

safety.model: Cloned human β1/β2 selectivity + anaesthetised-rat haemodynamics
safety.note: 24-h ambulatory BP and heart rate unchanged on solabegron in OAB women, as the selectivity assays and rat haemodynamics predicted.
safety.quote: There were no significant treatment differences for mean changes from baseline to week 8 in systolic blood pressure (BP), diastolic BP, mean arterial pressure (MAP), or heart rate during the 24-h ambulatory measurement.
safety.judgement: Abstract-level; the comparison is juxtaposed (selectivity model vs patient ABPM), not stated by the source. The mirabegron caveat: the thorough-QT study in healthy volunteers (Malik 2012, doi 10.1038/clpt.2012.181) found no QTcI prolongation at 50 or 100 mg but prolongation at 200 mg in females, and the label carries a blood-pressure warning for small HR/BP rises; no primary source characterises the models as having missed this, and the FDA nonclinical review (rat/monkey telemetry) could not be retrieved within budget (WebFetch size limit; browser-UA curl denied), so a stricter scorer may call it a scaling miss rather than same. Vibegron ABPM in patients (Weber 2022, doi 10.1097/MBP.0000000000000572, print 2022): 'no statistically significant or clinically relevant effects on BP or HR', consistent; its NCT was not looked up. Hatanaka 2013 note: mirabegron has intrinsic activity 0.6 at cloned rat β1 (EC50 610 nM) versus 0.1 at human β1, so rat haemodynamics over-predict β1 liability for this compound.
